facts.text: Plymouth is a city in Wayne County that is surrounded by, but independent of, Plymouth Township.
Kellogg Park, with its fountain, is the center of downtown Plymouth and a popular place to gather for concerts and events.
Just outside downtown, Plymouth has traditional neighborhood streets with sidewalks, mature trees and well-kept homes.
In 1871 George Starkweather built a store at the corner of Liberty and Starkweather and opened a road through his property for other stores; the area is now known as Old Village, or Lowertown.
Plymouth was settled in 1825, incorporated in 1867 and became a city in 1932.

The Plymouth Community Chamber of Commerce's Walk of Trees fills Kellogg Park with Christmas trees decorated by participants chosen by lottery, each tree supplied with 300 white lights; the 2025 display was open around the clock from November 28 through January 4.

The City of Plymouth's approved 2026 downtown events include a Main Street boulevard lighting in November, the Walk of Trees in Kellogg Park, and Santa's City of Plymouth Parade, which ends at Kellogg Park ahead of the Kellogg Park tree lighting.
The Plymouth Ice Festival held its 44th annual edition from January 30 to February 1, 2026, lining downtown Plymouth sidewalks with ice carvings.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Plymouth, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Plymouth Christmas light installation: tree wraps for mature trees, clean rooflines and porch lighting, with in-season service and takedown.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Plymouth, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Tree wraps, rooflines and porch lighting for homes on sidewalk-lined streets, from design and installation to in-season service and takedown.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Just outside downtown, Plymouth's neighborhood streets have sidewalks, mature trees and well-kept homes. That combination shapes a good display. People pass your house on foot, close enough to notice clean lines and uneven ones. And a mature tree in the front yard is often the strongest thing you can light. We wrap trunks and major limbs, light the canopy when the tree calls for it, and reach the upper branches from a bucket truck where the street and lot allow. The roofline, porch and shrubs then tie the house to the tree. We design it with you, install it, keep it lit through the season and take it down once the holidays are over.
considerations: Wrap the tree or light the canopy

Tight trunk and limb wraps give a tailored, glowing silhouette. Canopy lighting drapes the crown for a softer effect. Mature trees can take either, and we recommend one based on the species, the height and how the tree is seen from the sidewalk.

Tall trees near the curb are often easiest to reach from the street, which means planning around parked cars and overhead lines. We check both during the estimate and plan the install around parking and foot traffic on your block.

Downtown Plymouth lights its Main Street boulevard in November, and Santa's parade ends at Kellogg Park ahead of the tree lighting. If you want the house glowing by then, an early request gives you the most room on the schedule.
faq: Do you install Christmas lights in Plymouth Township as well as the city?

Yes. We serve the City of Plymouth and the township that surrounds it. Send your address with the request form or call (248) 756-8915 to set up a free estimate at your home, with a layout planned for your house and trees.
How many lights does a mature tree need?

It depends on the trunk, the spread of the limbs and the look you want. We measure the tree during the estimate and plan the wrap spacing from there, so the estimate reflects your tree rather than a rule of thumb.
When do the lights come down?

After the holidays. Takedown is scheduled with you, and if you would like the display to stay up a little longer into winter, mention it when you book so it can be planned. Everything comes down with care, and the yard goes back to normal.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Plymouth, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Outlines, window framing, tree wraps and bistro lights for downtown Plymouth storefronts, offices and managed properties, from walkthrough to removal.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Plymouth, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Storefront outlines, window framing, tree wraps and bistro lighting for downtown businesses, offices and the property managers who run them.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Downtown Plymouth centers on Kellogg Park and its fountain, and the holiday calendar there runs long. The Main Street boulevard lighting comes in November. Santa's City of Plymouth Parade ends at Kellogg Park ahead of the tree lighting. In 2025, the Walk of Trees display was open around the clock from November 28 through January 4, and the 2026 Ice Festival lined downtown sidewalks with carvings from January 30 to February 1. For a storefront, that is a long season to look right after dark. We design outlines, window framing, tree wraps and bistro lighting for that kind of attention. Bucket-truck crews hang it, a service call handles anything that goes dark along the way, and removal comes on a date agreed in the estimate.
considerations: A season that runs past New Year's

Downtown events run from the November boulevard lighting through the Walk of Trees and into the new year. If you want your display up for part of that stretch, tell us at the walkthrough so removal is planned to match.

Through the holidays, the Walk of Trees fills Kellogg Park with decorated trees, each supplied with 300 white lights. A storefront near the park is seen against that glow, so a crisp white outline and lit windows sit comfortably beside it, while strong color stands apart. Decide at the walkthrough which you want.

Offices, medical buildings and multi-tenant properties often suit a steady, simple display: clean outlines, lit entry trees and a welcoming front door. If you manage more than one address, the buildings can share one design so they read as a set.
faq: Can you light a storefront near Kellogg Park?

Yes. Downtown Plymouth is within our service area. Storefront work starts with a free walkthrough to see the facade, the trees out front and where a lift can safely set up, then an estimate that spells out design, installation, in-season service and removal.
Can our display stay up through the Ice Festival?

It can be planned. Removal comes after the season, on a timing settled with you in the estimate. The Ice Festival runs in late January or early February, so if you want the lights up that long, raise it at the walkthrough and the removal date can be set around it.
Do you handle offices and association entrances in Plymouth Township?

Yes. The township is within our service area, and we light offices, shopping centers, subdivision entrances and HOA common areas. Each project starts with a walkthrough and a written estimate the owner, manager or board can sign off on.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Plymouth, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent Christmas lights for Plymouth homes: a discreet track under the eaves, run from your phone, lit for evening walks and the holidays.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: Roofline lighting that stays up all year and answers to your phone: a quiet outline for evening walks past the house, full color when the holidays arrive.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: On Plymouth's sidewalk-lined neighborhood streets, a house is seen at walking pace most evenings of the year, not only in December. Permanent lighting fits that rhythm. A discreet track follows the roofline under the eaves and stays up all year, and the app on your phone sets the color and the schedule: warm white accent light most nights, a full Christmas scene once the Walk of Trees fills Kellogg Park, your team's colors on game day. Before anything is installed, we measure the roofline and plan the corners, the runs and where the power comes from.
considerations: Mature trees close to the house can shade part of the roofline or brush against the eaves. We look at branch clearance during the estimate and place the runs where the lights stay visible from the street and the sidewalk.
The look you will see most

Plan for the setting you will live with day to day. For many homes that is a simple warm white outline, with color saved for holidays and game days, so we lay out the runs to make that everyday look clean.

On a street with sidewalks, people are out at dusk and after dinner. Set the outline to come on at sunset and switch off at an hour you choose, so the house is lit when neighbors pass and dark once the street goes quiet. Schedules live in the app and can change whenever you like.
faq: Can I still have a tree wrapped for Christmas?

Yes. The permanent track covers the roofline, and a seasonal wrap for a mature front-yard tree can be added each season as a separate service. We can plan both together so the colors work with each other, and the estimate lists each one.
What condition does my roofline need to be in?

Sound enough to hold the track. It mounts along the fascia under the eaves, so we check the condition of that trim during the estimate and point out anything that should be addressed before installation.

Yes. It reflects your house rather than a package: the length of the roofline, the number of corners and peaks, and where power can be reached. The written estimate spells out what the installation includes.
